name: Single endpoint no link - daisy chain issue
description: User has no network on PC but VoIP phone works on same jack. Extracted from TKT-2026-00101.

questions.text: Does the VoIP phone on the same jack work?
questions.help_text: If phone is fine, the jack and main cable are OK. Isolates to the PC end.

questions.text: Check the switch port. Is the PC's MAC address in the MAC table?
questions.help_text: MAC absence suggests the PC isn't sending frames. Could be cable or NIC.

questions.text: Swap the patch cable between phone and PC. Does PC get DHCP?
questions.help_text: Cable swap isolates cable vs. NIC vs. daisy-chain termination.

fix_reseat_cable.title: Reseat the daisy-chain cable
steps: Unplug the PC-side pigtail connector completely
Reseat it firmly until the clip locks with an audible click
Verify DHCP lease on PC (run ipconfig /all)
Confirm access to network resources (ping gateway, open CRM)
Monitor for 5 minutes; if stable, close ticket

escalate_driver_issue.title: Escalate: NIC driver or endpoint issue
steps: Cable and jack are healthy, MAC not appearing
Likely NIC driver failure or endpoint hardware fault
Escalate to endpoint support or replace device

escalate_endpoint_nic.title: Escalate: Endpoint NIC or daisy chain termination
steps: PC still offline even after cable swap
Likely NIC hardware issue or damaged phone-end termination
Swap with a known-good phone or replace PC endpoint

escalate_jack_faulty.title: Escalate: Jack or patch panel fault
steps: Both PC and phone offline on same jack
Jack or patch panel port is faulty
Contact facilities to re-punch the jack or swap patch panel port

name: Multi-user outage on single switch - LAG member down
description: Entire pod (8+ users) loses data and voice simultaneously. Indicates switch failure or backbone link issue. Extracted from TKT-2026-00102.

questions.text: Which users/pods are affected? (e.g. POD-3: 8 people, or POD-1,2,3: 24 people)
Which switch do all affected users patch into? (e.g. SW-B-02)
Check the Meraki dashboard. What is the switch's uplink status?
questions.help_text: Flapping or red uplink is catastrophic for all downstream users.

questions.text: Uplink is green. Check switch VLAN config. Are VLANs 10, 20 allowed on the uplink trunk?
questions.help_text: Config drift: VLAN was removed from trunk after maintenance.

questions.text: Uplink is flapping. Console to the switch. How many LAG members are UP?
questions.help_text: One LAG member down halves capacity; two down is total loss.

questions.text: Both LAG members are UP but link is flapping. Check packet loss on uplink. Is it > 5%?
questions.help_text: High packet loss on green link suggests SFP transceiver issues.

fix_reseat_fiber.title: Reseat the fibre strand in RACK-A
steps: Go to RACK-A main comms room
Locate the fibre uplink pair terminating this switch's LAG
Check both strands: note which is down (usually LED dark on transceiver)
Carefully remove the down strand from its SFP transceiver
Reseat it firmly until it clicks; LED should light within 30 seconds
Watch console: LAG should negotiate and both members come UP
Monitor traffic from this pod for 20 minutes to confirm stability
If only one strand was down, capacity degradation is expected until partner strand is back

fix_add_vlans.title: Add missing VLANs to uplink trunk
steps: Enter switch config for the uplink trunk port
Add VLAN 10 (STAFF_DATA) and VLAN 20 (VOIP) to allowed list
Commit and verify: users should regain connectivity within 30 seconds
Check a few endpoints for DHCP lease

escalate_firewall.title: Escalate: Firewall or upstream issue
steps: Switch config is correct, uplink is green, VLANs are allowed, but pod still down
Firewall may have blocking rule, or upstream circuit is failed
Check firewall logs for drop rules matching this VLAN/pod
If firewall rules are clean, escalate to WAN provider

escalate_no_uplink.title: Escalate: Complete uplink failure
steps: Switch uplink is completely down (red)
Entire pod is isolated
Check RACK-A for fibre break, tranceiver failure, or cable disconnection
If physically OK, escalate to provider for backbone circuit failure

escalate_backbone_cable.title: Escalate: Both LAG members down
steps: Both fibre strands in this LAG are down (none up)
Backbone cable cut or both transceivers failed
Entire pod (potentially multiple racks) affected
Escalate to facilities/provider immediately

escalate_sfp_error.title: Escalate: Transceiver flap
steps: LAG members reporting UP but link keeps dropping
Likely SFP transceiver firmware issue or dirty optic
Swap the suspect SFP transceiver with a known-good one
If problem persists, escalate to hardware support

name: Jack label mismatch - physical termination vs. faceplate label
description: Faceplate sticker says one jack ID, but cable actually terminates in a different jack. Extracted from TKT-2026-00103.

questions.text: User reports jack label mismatch. What does the FACEPLATE sticker say?
Physically trace the cable from the faceplate. Where does it ACTUALLY terminate in the patch panel?
Does the actual termination match the faceplate label?
questions.help_text: Mismatch means either the jack was re-punched or the sticker was mislabeled.

fix_update_topology.title: Update topology and relabel faceplate
steps: In Bubba's topology.json, update wall_jack.jack_label to match ACTUAL termination
Update the faceplate label sticker to match reality
Re-run topology validation to ensure all cross-references still resolve
Confirm user can now reference the desk/jack correctly in future tickets
Document this as a known labelling issue in the office notes (may indicate other mismatches)

escalate_why_reported.title: Escalate: Why did user report mismatch if sticker is correct?
steps: If topology and reality match, user may be confused about which jack they're at
Confirm with user they're testing the correct desk
Check actual symptom - is there a connectivity issue, or just labelling confusion?

name: Conference room cable unplugged - user or cleaner disconnect
description: Shared conference room system offline. Usually caused by cable being unplugged by cleaning crew or during setup. Extracted from TKT-2026-00109.

questions.text: Go to the conference room. Is the ethernet cable plugged into the system?
questions.help_text: Conference room cables are frequently pulled by cleaners or during room setup.

questions.text: Cable is plugged in. Is there a link light on the endpoint NIC?
questions.help_text: Link light means physical connection; no light means cable is bad or port is down.

fix_replug_cable.title: Replug the ethernet cable
steps: Locate the ethernet cable at the back of the conference system
If unplugged, firmly insert it into the RJ45 port until it clicks
Wait 20 seconds for the system to negotiate DHCP
Verify: link light comes on, system responds to ping
Test booking system if applicable

fix_swap_cable.title: Swap the ethernet cable
steps: The cable is plugged but no link light; cable is likely damaged
Bring a spare cat6 cable from the supplies closet
Replace and verify link light and DHCP
If successful, dispose of damaged cable and order replacement

escalate_dhcp.title: Escalate: Link OK but no DHCP
steps: Link light is on, but system has no IP
Check DHCP scope for this VLAN (check switch port VLAN assignment)
If scope is available, power-cycle the endpoint
If cycle doesn't help, check for IP conflicts in DHCP logs

graph_references: switch_port.vlan_id (check DHCP scope for this VLAN)

name: VoIP phone registration failure - voice VLAN not on trunk
description: IP phone fails SIP registration. Switch port has data VLAN only; voice VLAN not tagged. Extracted from TKT-2026-00111.

questions.text: Does the phone have a link light (physical connection)?
Does the phone have an IP address on its display?
questions.help_text: If no DHCP, the phone is on data VLAN only (VLAN 10), no access to management VLAN.

questions.text: Can you reach the SIP server from the phone's IP? (Verify in phone menu or ping from CLI)
questions.help_text: If SIP server is unreachable, phone and server are on different VLANs with no routing.

fix_add_voice_vlan.title: Add voice VLAN (20) to the switch port
steps: Locate the switch port this phone is patched into (check topology)
SSH to the switch and enter config for that port
Change the port to 'access' mode with VLAN 20 (VOIP)
Or if trunk: add VLAN 20 to the allowed VLAN list
Save and commit
Wait 30 seconds; phone should re-register
Verify: phone displays registered status, can make test call

escalate_sip_config.title: Escalate: SIP server config issue
steps: Phone can reach SIP server but refuses to register
Check phone SIP config (correct server FQDN/IP, port 5060)
Check PBX/SIP server logs for auth failures
If config matches, escalate to VoIP provider

escalate_cable.title: Escalate: No link light
steps: Phone has no link light; physical connection is broken
Swap cable at desk; if no link, the jack or switch port is faulty

escalate_dhcp_data_vlan.title: Escalate: DHCP on data VLAN only
steps: Phone got DHCP but only on VLAN 10 (data), not VLAN 20 (voice)
Check switch port config: should be access VLAN 20 or trunk with both VLANs
Or check DHCP scope for VLAN 20: is there an available range?

graph_references: switch_port.mode (access vs trunk), vlan_id, allowed_vlans (should include 20)

name: AD group mismatch after promotion - recurring pattern
description: User promoted to new role but AD group membership not updated. Access to role-based resources fails. Extracted from TKT-2026-00123. This is the 4th occurrence.

questions.text: Was the user recently promoted or assigned a new role?
What AD groups is the user currently in? (Query AD or ask user to run 'whoami /groups')
What is the AD group for the new role? (e.g. Team_Leaders, QA_Analysts)
Is the user in the NEW role group?

fix_add_new_group.title: Add user to new role's AD group
steps: Open Active Directory Users and Computers
Find the new role's group (e.g. Team_Leaders, QA_Analysts)
Add the user to this group
Proceed to fix_remove_old_group to clean up
fix_add_new_group.preventive: This is the 4th occurrence in 6 months. Escalate to HR: implement automated AD provisioning on promotion events in HRIS.

fix_remove_old_group.title: Remove user from old role's AD group
steps: Find the OLD role group (e.g. Customer_Service_Advisors)
Remove the user from this group (check HR policy: some require async removal after 30 days)
Force gpupdate /force on user's device
Verify: user can now access new-role resources

escalate_not_promotion.title: Escalate: Access issue not related to promotion
steps: User reports access denied but not recently promoted
Check: is the user in the required AD group?
If yes, escalate to resource owner (shared drive, application)
If no, investigate why user was removed from group

graph_references: department (Team Leadership) → role group (Team_Leaders, QA_Analysts, etc.)
notes: Pattern indicates HR → IT provisioning gap. Recommend automated AD updates on HRIS role changes.

name: Cable unseated at desk - cleaning crew or user unplugging
description: Both PC and phone offline at a desk. Usually the ethernet cable was unplugged by user or cleaning crew. Extracted from TKT-2026-00118. Recurring with T109.

questions.text: Go to the desk. Is the ethernet cable plugged into the wall jack?
questions.help_text: Cleaning crew often unplugs cables under desks accidentally.

questions.text: Cable is plugged in. Is there a link light on the PC NIC?
PC has link. Does the phone display an IP address?

fix_replug_cable.title: Replug the ethernet cable
steps: Unplug the cable completely from the wall jack
Reseat it firmly until it clicks
Wait 20 seconds for devices to negotiate DHCP
Verify: both PC and phone have connectivity (ping, test CRM access)
Confirm with user; close ticket

fix_swap_cable.title: Swap the ethernet cable
steps: Cable is plugged but no link light; cable is likely damaged
Get a spare cat6 cable
Replace and verify link light comes on within 10 seconds
Dispose of damaged cable

fix_power_cycle_phone.title: Power-cycle the VoIP phone
steps: PC has link but phone shows no IP
Unplug phone power for 10 seconds
Plug back in and wait for registration
Phone should display IP and registered status within 30 seconds

escalate_vlan_routing.title: Escalate: VLAN isolation issue
steps: Both PC and phone have IPs/link but no actual connectivity
Suggests VLAN routing issue or firewall blocking
Check switch port is carrying both VLANs 10 and 20

notes: Same root cause as T109. Consider placing 'Do Not Unplug' labels on conference room and desk cables.

name: Open ticket - partial diagnosis, awaiting external data
description: CTI (computer telephony integration) sync issue, sporadic, requires partner logs to diagnose. Extracted from TKT-2026-00125. Demonstrates escalation when data is unavailable.

questions.text: What is your current hypothesis for the cause?
What data have you collected so far?
What external data or partner access do you need to proceed?

document_hypothesis.title: Document and await
steps: Record the current hypothesis clearly in the ticket
List all data collected and results
Specify exactly what external data is needed (e.g. Harbourline CRM logs between time X and Y)
Create a follow-up reminder for 2 business days
Escalate to partner contact if data hasn't arrived
